narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story of Israel in Egypt and the call of Moses.

moses.name: Moses
moses.note: Hebrew raised in Pharaoh's house, shepherd in Madian; hesitant and awed before God, pleading for his people.

pharaoh.name: Pharaoh
pharaoh.note: King of Egypt; calculating, haughty and harsh toward the Hebrews.

moses-and-aaron.name: Moses and Aaron
moses-and-aaron.note: The two brothers delivering the Lord's message to Pharaoh together; firm, respectful.

taskmasters.name: Pharaoh's overseers and taskmasters
taskmasters.note: Egyptian slave-drivers passing on the order about straw; brutal, barking.

israelites.name: Officers of the children of Israel
israelites.note: Hebrew foremen, beaten for the brick quota; pleading before Pharaoh, then bitter toward Moses and Aaron.

1.t: After these things, Moses and Aaron went in, and said to Pharao:
Thus saith the Lord God of Israel: Let my people go, that they may sacrifice to me in the desert.
1.q: text says Moses and Aaron said it together; could be given to aaron alone as the spokesman (4:16)

2.t: Who is the Lord, that I should hear his voice, and let Israel go? I know not the Lord, neither will I let Israel go.

3.t: The God of the Hebrews hath called us, to go three days' journey into the wilderness, and to sacrifice to the Lord our God; lest a pestilence or the sword fall upon us.
3.q: text says Moses and Aaron said it together; could be given to aaron alone as the spokesman (4:16)

4.t: The king of Egypt said to them:
Why do you Moses and Aaron draw off the people from their works? Get you gone to your burdens.

5.t: The people of the land are numerous; you see that the multitude is increased; how much more if you give them rest from their works?

6.t: Therefore he commanded the same day the overseers of the works, and the task-masters of the people, saying:

7.t: You shall give straw no more to the people to make brick, as before; but let them go and gather straw.

8.t: And you shall lay upon them the task of bricks, which they did before; neither shall you diminish any thing thereof, for they are idle, and therefore they cry. saying: Let us go and sacrifice to our God.

9.t: Let them be oppressed with works, and let them fulfil them; that they may not regard lying words.

10.t: And the overseers of the works, and the taskmasters, went out and said to the people:
Thus saith Pharao: I allow you no straw;

11.t: Go, and gather it where you can find it; neither shall any thing of your work be diminished.

12.t: And the people was scattered through all the land of Egypt to gather straw.

13.t: And the overseers of the works pressed them, saying:
Fulfil your work every day, as before ye were wont to do, when straw was given you.

14.t: And they that were over the works of the children of Israel, were scourged by Pharao's taskmasters, saying:
Why have you not made up the task of bricks, both yesterday and to day, as before?

15.t: And the officers of the children of Israel came, and cried out to Pharao, saying:
Why dealest thou so with thy servants?

16.t: Straw is not given us, and bricks are required of us as before; behold we, thy servants, are beaten with whips, and thy people is unjustly dealt withal.

17.t: You are idle, and therefore you say: Let us go and sacrifice to the Lord.

18.t: Go therefore and work: straw shall not be given you, and you shall deliver the accustomed number of bricks.

19.t: And the officers of the children of Israel saw that they were in evil case, because it was said to them:
There shall not a whit be diminished of the bricks for every day.
19.q: quoted order reported in the passive inside narration ("it was said to them"); kept with the narrator rather than pharaoh or taskmasters

20.t: And they met Moses and Aaron, who stood over against them as they came out from Pharao:

21.t: The Lord see and judge, because you have, made our savour to stink before Pharao and his servants, and you have given him a sword, to kill us.

22.t: And Moses returned to the Lord, and said:
Lord, why hast thou afflicted this people? wherefore hast thou sent me?

23.t: For since the time that I went in to Pharao to speak in thy name, he hath afflicted thy people: and thou hast not delivered them.
